observations.title: Session summary: stock-controll
observations.content:
## Goal
Refactorizar y blindar el motor de descuentos, estabilizar la interfaz del POS (NewSale y modal) y arreglar errores fatales en el guardado de cajas (cashRegisters y movements).

## Instructions
El usuario tiene una política inquebrantable: "El frontend NUNCA debe hacer cálculos financieros, solo el backend". Además, los reportes deben almacenar el subtotal bruto crudo para estadísticas y un total neto transaccional. Estas reglas rigen todo el desarrollo.

## Discoveries
- El cálculo de "tope de descuentos" en cascada fracasaba por achicamiento geométrico. Si el tope era 50% ($50) sobre $100, y se aplicaba 50% ($50), el segundo descuento (ej. 10%) operaba sobre el remanente ($50) dando $5 (totalizando $55). Solución: evaluar el 'nominalImpact' sobre el monto crudo base y llevar el acumulador validándolo contra el tope permitido, podando ramas secuenciales.
- La validación `validatePayments` fallaba en `salesServices` porque el front armaba el payload `paymentBreakdown` tomando el valor crudo en vez del neto con descuento.
- Prisma revoca las creaciones planas escalares en relaciones (ej. `openedByUserId` y `cashRegisterId`) tirando un 'Argument missing must not be null' en las creaciones/actualizaciones de Caja. Hay que usar el conector relacional `connect: { id }`.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Rediseñamos el engine paramétrico de descuentos para hacer un 'Slot Management' y evitar superar jamás el 50% max limit configurado mediante un algoritmo determinista iterativo por capas de reglas (preferred, layer, impacto_desc).
- ✅ Refactorizado el POS UI (`DiscountSummaryModal.jsx` y `NewSale.jsx`) agregando scrolls, limitando alturas y permitiendo expandir/colapsar el warning de límites/intercambiabilidad. 
- ✅ Implementación del "Neto Sincronizado": el frontend agarra `discountPreview.finalTotal` y forma automágicamente el breakdown del pago, evitando mutaciones del front y asegurando que las ventas no truenen en el backend.
- ✅ Modificados `cajaServices.js` y `movimientosServices.js` para usar sintaxis estricta de Prisma (`connect: { id: user.id }`), reparando los crash blockings al abrir/cerrar caja y crear movimientos de efectivo.

## Relevant Files
- services/discountService.js — Cálculo e impacto atómico de motor de descuentos. Validación de tope basada en nominalImpacts.
- src/pages/sales/NewSale.jsx — Lógica reformada del frontend POS que respeta 'cálculos 0' y asume el finalTotal dictado por middleware para el formulario paymentBreakdown.
- services/cajaServices.js — Sintaxis estricta de Prisma para relations y control defensivo de storeId.
- services/movimientosServices.js — Relaciones en modo `connect` para cashRegister y user.
- CONTEXT-HANDOVER.md — Documentado extenso el update de refactorización total del proyecto de la sesión de hoy.

observations.title: Prisma Strict Relation Syntax in Create/Update
observations.content:
**What**: Prisma throws "Argument missing must not be null" for relation paths even if the scalar ID variables are provided in `create()` operations. Updated all cash register related writes to use explicit `connect`.
**Why**: Prisma changed relationship persistence enforcement. Setting scalar properties directly (`cashRegisterId: "abc"`) causes fatal DB operation errors; requires nested relation configuration.
**Where**: services/cajaServices.js, services/movimientosServices.js
**Learned**: ALWAYS use the `{ connect: { id: "123" } }` nested structure syntax when creating or updating models with relational foreign keys in Prisma instead of direct scalar variable injection.

observations.title: Cálculo Atómico de Tope de Descuentos
observations.content:
**What**: Se rediseñó el procesamiento de descuentos para evitar fugas en el tope (maxPct) por "reducción en cascada", sumando los impactos nominales generados en vez del resultado del acumulador subtotal con descuentos aplicados.
**Why**: Cuando se apilan reglas iterativas, el saldo disminuye y la matemática porcentual permite que se cuelen reglas superando el límite real sobre el monto crudo original.
**Where**: services/discountService.js (función mergeEngineResults)
**Learned**: Para un Slot Management estricto, o limitadores de cuota o topes duros de venta, siempre hay que calcular el `nominalImpact` basándose en el precio crudo inmutable desde el inicio de la operación, sin achicar la base de cálculo en etapas intermedias.

**Why**: Permite al usuario SISTEMA testear la UI desde la perspectiva de otros roles sin cambiar de cuenta.
**Where**: 
- Back: authMiddleware.js (inyecta simulatedRole si es SISTEMA), rbacMiddleware.js (forwarding), rbacService.js (checkPermission con simulatedRole).
- Front: userStore.js (simulatedRole persistido en localStorage), axiosSetup.js (inyecta x-simulated-role header), sidebar.jsx (selector 🎭), MainLayout.jsx (effectiveRole = simulatedRole || user.role).
**Learned**: La visibilidad del selector usa user.role REAL (no simulatedRole) para garantizar que siempre esté visible. El backend valida primero el JWT antes de procesar el header x-simulated-role. Logs de auditoría deben marcarse como "Simulada por SISTEMA" — pendiente de implementar en cada servicio que loguee.

## Goal
Investigar y corregir la falla de seguridad que permitió realizar una venta sin tienda seleccionada y finalizar el sistema de simulación de roles.

## Instructions
- Los usuarios SISTEMA deben tener trazabilidad completa en las acciones simuladas.
- Las validaciones de integridad de tienda deben ocurrir en el authMiddleware para proteger todos los servicios.

## Discoveries
- **Falla de Seguridad**: El authMiddleware confiaba en el `storeId` persistido en el JWT (stateless), lo que permitía "ghost storeIds" si el perfil del usuario cambiaba en la DB pero no se re-logueaba.
- **Validación Crucial**: Un rol operativo simulado (VENDEDOR/ENCARGADO) debe estar asociado obligatoriamente a un contexto de tienda física, de lo contrario las acciones de caja/ventas fallan o corrompen datos.

## Accomplished
- ✅ **Sincronización Real-time**: El `authMiddleware` ahora refresca el `storeId` desde la DB en cada petición, invalidando datos obsoletos del JWT.
- ✅ **Blindaje Global**: Se fuerza `storeId: null` para usuarios SISTEMA en modo "ALL", impidiendo operaciones físicas accidentales.
- ✅ **Bloqueo de Simulación Inconsistente**: Se rechaza la activación de roles operativos si el usuario no ha seleccionado una tienda activa.
- ✅ **Trazabilidad**: Se agregó la etiqueta "(Simulada por SISTEMA)" a los logs de Stock, Caja y Movimientos.

## Next Steps
- Realizar pruebas de estrés sobre el rbacService para asegurar que no hay fugas de permisos en otros módulos (Productos, Clientes).

## Relevant Files
- `middlewares/authMiddleware.js` — Lógica central de sincronización de storeId y validación de simulación.
- `services/salesServices.js` — Auditoría de ventas simuladas.

observations.title: Blindaje de Integridad de Tienda y Simulación de Roles
observations.content:
**What**: Sincronización obligatoria de `storeId` desde la DB en el `authMiddleware` y bloqueo de simulación operativa sin tienda.
**Why**: Se detectó que un usuario SISTEMA podía realizar ventas sin tienda seleccionada debido a que el JWT conservaba un `storeId` antiguo.

**Learned**: No se debe confiar en los datos de contexto (como storeId) persistidos en un JWT si el usuario tiene permisos para cambiar de contexto dinámicamente. Siempre re-validar contra la DB o forzar null según el header de contexto.

## Goal
Resolver el bloqueo del "Sudo Mode" en la creación de usuarios administradores tras el despliegue distribuido (Vercel + Render + Supabase).

## Instructions
- Se estableció que para entornos Cross-Site (Vercel -> Render), las cookies DEBEN usar `SameSite=None` y `Secure=True`.
- Se configuró el backend para alternar automáticamente entre `lax` (desarrollo) y `none` (producción) basado en `NODE_ENV`.

## Discoveries
- El "Sudo Mode" fallaba porque la cookie `sudo` se emitía con `SameSite: Strict` en lugar de usar el helper global, lo que impedía que el navegador la enviara en peticiones originadas desde el frontend de Vercel.
- El usuario ya tenía implementado un fallback de headers para el token de sesión, lo que ocultaba el problema de las cookies hasta que se intentaba usar una funcionalidad que dependía exclusivamente de ellas (como el Sudo Mode).

## Accomplished
- ✅ Se actualizó `buildCookieOptions` en `authController.js` para soportar `SameSite: 'none'` en producción.
- ✅ Se corrigió el endpoint `verifySudo` para utilizar `buildCookieOptions` en lugar de una configuración manual restrictiva.
- ✅ Se estandarizó la limpieza de cookies en `logout` usando el mismo helper.

## Relevant Files

observations.title: Fixed Prisma UncheckedCreateInput object mixture bug
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed Prisma Invalid invocation error when creating employee
**Why**: The code was mixing a relational connect object (`store: { connect: ... }`) with a scalar foreign key (`roleId: string`). When passing a scalar foreign key directly, Prisma infers the payload type as `UncheckedCreateInput`. In this unchecked mode, relational objects (`store`) are invalid; it expects the scalar `storeId`.
**Where**: e:\proyects\stock-controll-back\services\employeeServices.js
**Learned**: Never mix scalar foreign keys and relational object connects in Prisma payloads. If you use one scalar ID, use scalars for all relations (e.g. `storeId` instead of `store: {connect}`).

observations.title: sdd/refactor-details-jsx/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Refactor Details.jsx

## Intent
Dismantle the 1100+ line "God Component" `Details.jsx` to improve maintainability, enforce Single Responsibility Principle (SRP), and modernize the UI/UX with better loading states and structured layouts.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Extract configuration and hardcoded rules to a separate file.
- Extract data fetching and saving logic to custom hooks (`useEntityData`, `useEntitySave`).
- Extract UI elements into modular sub-components (`EntityHeader`, `EntityForm`, `BarcodePreview`).
- Implement Skeleton loaders for better UX.

### Out of Scope
- Changing backend API endpoints.
- Modifying routing paths.
- Changing global theme system.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- None

### Modified Capabilities
- None

## Approach
1. Move constants (`ENTITY_ALLOWED_ROLES`, `ENTITY_FIELD_RULES`) to `src/config/entityRules.js`.
2. Create custom hooks in `src/hooks/` to handle fetching, saving, and role checks.
3. Create sub-components in `src/components/Details/` (e.g., Header, Form, Actions).
4. Recompose `Details.jsx` using these new modular pieces.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `src/pages/Details.jsx` | Modified | Core component being refactored |
| `src/config/entityRules.js` | New | Extracted configurations |
| `src/hooks/useEntityData.js` | New | Extracted fetch logic |
| `src/hooks/useEntitySave.js` | New | Extracted save logic |
| `src/components/Details/*` | New | Extracted UI components |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Breaking entity-specific logic (e.g., users vs products) | Medium | Rigorous manual testing per entity type. |
| Losing unsaved changes | Low | Mirroring existing state guard `isSaving`. |

## Rollback Plan
Revert via Git to the commit prior to the start of the refactor.

## Dependencies
- None

## Success Criteria
- [ ] `Details.jsx` is under 300 lines of code.
- [ ] Logic is cleanly separated into reusable hooks.
- [ ] UI displays skeleton loaders during initial fetch.
- [ ] All previous entity actions (edit, active toggle, print) work without regressions.

observations.title: Extracted entity rules to config file
observations.content:
**What**: Extracted `ENTITY_ALLOWED_ROLES` and `ENTITY_FIELD_RULES` to `src/config/entityRules.js`.
**Why**: To reduce the size of `Details.jsx` and follow the principle of separation of concerns, moving configuration out of the component.
**Where**: `src/config/entityRules.js`
**Learned**: Centralizing these rules makes it easier to add new entities or modify permissions without touching the main UI logic.

observations.title: Created useEntityData hook
observations.content:
**What**: Created `useEntityData` hook.
**Why**: To isolate API fetching logic from the UI. This hook handles loading states, entity-specific side data (categories for products, product counts for categories), and error handling.
**Where**: `src/hooks/useEntityData.js`
**Learned**: Using `useCallback` for `fetchData` ensures it can be passed safely to other hooks or components without causing infinite render loops if used in `useEffect`.

observations.title: Created useEntitySave hook
observations.content:
**What**: Created `useEntitySave` hook.
**Why**: To extract the massive `performSave` logic from `Details.jsx`. This hook handles the multi-step process of saving entity data, stock adjustments, and a queue of image operations (delete, upload, set_main).
**Where**: `src/hooks/useEntitySave.js`
**Learned**: Breaking down complex state transitions into a dedicated hook makes the UI component much more declarative and easier to test. It also prevents "race conditions" using a `ref` for the saving state.

observations.title: Extracted UI components for Details refactor
observations.content:
**What**: Completed extraction of UI sub-components for `Details.jsx`.
**Why**: To implement a modular, presentational architecture. This separates the layout and rendering logic from the state management, making both easier to maintain.
**Where**: `src/pages/Details/components/*`
**Learned**: Moving the `renderValue` and `isExcluded` logic into `DynamicForm` significantly reduced the visual noise in the main `Details.jsx` component. Using a dedicated `SkeletonDetails` provides a much more premium feel during initial load.

observations.title: Renamed DynamicForm to EntityDetailsForm to prevent naming conflict
observations.content:
**What**: Renamed `Details/components/DynamicForm.jsx` to `Details/components/EntityDetailsForm.jsx`.
**Why**: There was already a `src/components/DynamicForm.jsx` (creation form with 434 lines). Using the same name in Details/components would create a serious naming ambiguity. The old DynamicForm.jsx now exports from EntityDetailsForm as a breadcrumb.
**Where**: `src/pages/Details/components/EntityDetailsForm.jsx`, `src/pages/Details/components/DynamicForm.jsx`
**Learned**: Always check for duplicate component names before creating new ones in a refactor. Even with different paths, identical names cause cognitive confusion. The new DynamicForm is a CREATION form, EntityDetailsForm is for VIEWING/EDITING details — completely different concerns.

observations.title: Completed Details.jsx assembly - Phase 3
observations.content:
**What**: Completed Phase 3 of the Details.jsx refactor. The main component now composes hooks and sub-components.
**Why**: To finalize the modular architecture. Details.jsx went from 1100+ lines to ~320 lines.
**Where**: `src/pages/Details.jsx`
**Learned**: 
- formData sync must use useEffect, NOT a conditional assignment during render (causes render loop warnings).
- EntityDetailsForm needed access to `data` (original) AND `formData` (editing state) for cases like stock display.
- The `role` select for `ROLES.SISTEMA` needed special handling preserved from original.
- `password` field renders a "Blanquear Clave" button in edit mode, NOT a text input.

observations.title: Fixed global RBAC normalization issue
observations.content:
**What**: Normalized all role-based access checks to use `.toUpperCase()` across the entire application.
**Why**: The application's RBAC system was failing intermittently because some components were comparing mixed-case roles (e.g., "Administrador") against uppercase constants (e.g., "ADMINISTRADOR"). This caused buttons to disappear or routes to be blocked even for high-privileged users.
**Where**: `Details.jsx`, `AccountList.jsx`, `MainPanel.jsx`, `DiscountsMainPage.jsx`, `MainLayout.jsx`, `GenericTableSection.jsx`.
**Learned**: Always normalize string identifiers used for security checks to a consistent case (usually uppercase) to prevent silent permission failures. This is especially important when using a "Role Simulation" feature where manual input might not match DB formatting.

observations.title: sdd/discount-partial-payment-fix/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Discount Partial Payments and Validation Fix

## Intent

Enable business flexibility by allowing discounts to be applied specifically to the portion of a sale paid with a certain method (e.g., 10% off only on the cash portion). Additionally, resolve a recurring bug where combined payments are rejected due to cent-level rounding differences between the frontend preview and backend final calculation.

## Scope

### In Scope
- **Database**: Add `allowPartialPayments` field to `DiscountRule` model.
- **Engine**: Extend Universal Engine to calculate discounts based on individual payment method amounts when `allowPartialPayments` is enabled.
- **Validation**: Refactor `validatePayments` in `salesServices.js` to allow the backend to "autofix" or tolerate cent-level rounding errors during finalization.
- **API**: Update sales and preview endpoints to accept full `paymentBreakdown` (method + amount).
- **UI**: Add `allowPartialPayments` checkbox to the discount creation form.

### Out of Scope
- Modifying the Legacy Discount Engine (it will remain as-is for backward compatibility).
- Changes to the automatic "Limited Stock" decrement logic beyond standard behavior.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities
- `discount-calculation`: Update to support amount-aware payment method filtering and prorated calculation.
- `discount-management`: Update to include the `allowPartialPayments` flag in rule configuration.

## Approach

1.  **Schema Update**: Add `allowPartialPayments Boolean @default(false)` to `DiscountRule`.
2.  **Engine Evolution**: 
    - Pass the full `paymentBreakdown` (with amounts) to the evaluator.
    - If `allowPartialPayments` is `true`, the `applicableSubtotal` for a rule is capped by the amount paid with the rule's permitted methods.
3.  **Validation Shield**: Update `salesServices.js` to prioritize backend-calculated totals and adjust the `paymentBreakdown` amounts for cent-level differences instead of throwing an error, as long as the user's intent matches the engine's calculation.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `prisma/schema.prisma` | Modified | Add `allowPartialPayments` to `DiscountRule`. |
| `services/discountEngine/universal/evaluator.js` | Modified | Update `validateTicketConditions` and `evaluateUniversal`. |
| `services/salesServices.js` | Modified | Update `create` and `validatePayments` logic. |
| `src/components/Discounts/DiscountFormModal.jsx` | Modified | Add checkbox for the new field. |
| `src/pages/sales/NewSale.jsx` | Modified | Update payload for preview and sale creation. |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Over-discounting on partial payments | Low | Strict math validation: `Discount <= Math.min(Subtotal, MethodAmount)`. |
| Database migration lock | Low | Small addition, non-breaking default value. |

## Rollback Plan

Revert `prisma/schema.prisma` changes (keep the column as optional or remove) and restore the previous versions of the service files.

## Dependencies

- Prisma migration is required.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Discounts can be applied specifically to the Cash portion of a combined payment.
- [ ] Combined payments with cent-level rounding differences no longer fail to process.
- [ ] The "Calcular Descuentos" modal correctly displays partial discount impacts.

# SDD Specs: discount-partial-payment-fix

## Domain: discount-calculation (Delta)

### MODIFIED Requirement: Global Ticket Guards
The system MUST NOT apply any discount if the transaction does not meet the rule's `ticketConditions`. If `allowPartialPayments` is enabled, the discount SHALL be applied only to the portion of the subtotal covered by the permitted methods. If disabled, the discount MUST NOT be applied if ANY portion uses a non-permitted method.
(Previously: The system MUST NOT apply any discount if the transaction does not meet the rule's `ticketConditions`.)

### ADDED Requirement: Payment Validation Tolerance
The system MUST allow a small monetary difference (tolerance) between backend and frontend totals (approx $0.01). The backend SHALL automatically adjust the breakdown to match the computed total.

## Domain: discount-management (Delta)

### ADDED Requirement: Partial Payment Configuration
The system MUST allow administrators to toggle the `allowPartialPayments` flag. Defaults to `false`.

observations.title: Proposal: Multi-Store Admin
observations.content:
# Proposal: Multi-Store Admin Access

## Intent
Allow an `ADMINISTRADOR` to manage multiple specific stores without having global access (`storeId = null`) like the `SISTEMA` role.

## Scope
- Add many-to-many relationship `allowedStores` in `schema.prisma`.
- Update `authMiddleware.js` to process `x-store-id` for `ADMINISTRADOR` and validate against `allowedStores`.
- Update `authServices.js` to return `allowedStores` array in the login payload.
- Update User ABM controller to accept and persist `allowedStoreIds` during creation/editing.

## Capabilities
- New: `multi-store-access`

## Approach
Implement a Clean Relational approach. Update the Prisma schema to include an implicit many-to-many relationship (`allowedStores store[] @relation("UserAllowedStores")`) on the `user` model. Modify the auth middleware to read the user's `allowedStores` from the DB and validate the `x-store-id` header against this list.

## Rollback Plan
1. Revert Git commit containing the middleware and schema changes.
2. Run `npx prisma db push` or revert the migration.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Admin user can login and receive their `allowedStores` list.
- [ ] Admin can send `x-store-id` matching an allowed store and get 200 OK.
- [ ] Admin sending `x-store-id` NOT in allowed stores gets 403 Forbidden.
- [ ] Non-admin users are strictly bound to their primary `storeId`.

observations.title: Spec: multi-store-admin
observations.content:
# multi-store-access Specification

## Purpose
Define the access control rules and dynamic store switching behavior for administrative users managing multiple stores.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Admin Multi-Store Authorization
The system MUST allow an `ADMINISTRADOR` to have a predefined list of allowed stores, and MUST restrict their operative context strictly to those stores.

#### Scenario: Admin accesses an allowed store
- GIVEN an `ADMINISTRADOR` with allowed stores [Store A, Store B]
- WHEN they send a request with header `x-store-id: Store B`
- THEN the system MUST authenticate the request under the context of Store B
- AND respond with HTTP 200 OK

#### Scenario: Admin attempts to access a forbidden store
- GIVEN an `ADMINISTRADOR` with allowed stores [Store A, Store B]
- WHEN they send a request with header `x-store-id: Store C`
- THEN the system MUST reject the context override
- AND respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden

#### Scenario: Operative user attempts to switch stores
- GIVEN a `VENDEDOR` assigned strictly to Store A
- WHEN they send a request with header `x-store-id: Store B`
- THEN the system MUST ignore the header
- AND force the execution context to Store A

### Requirement: Allowed Stores Delivery
The system MUST deliver the list of allowed stores to the client application upon successful login for authorized administrative roles.

#### Scenario: Admin logs in successfully
- GIVEN an active `ADMINISTRADOR` account
- WHEN they authenticate with valid credentials
- THEN the login payload MUST include an array of `allowedStores`
- AND the array MUST contain the `id` and `name` of each permitted store

## Goal
Investigar el error de Prisma en `AppliedDiscount.create` dentro de `stock-controll-back` y ubicar el desajuste exacto entre schema, servicio de ventas y motor de descuentos.

## Instructions

- `AppliedDiscount` en Prisma exige `type`, `layer`, `percentage`, `amount` y `reason`; `discountedQuantity` es opcional.

- Ese `type` universal representa capa, no `DiscountType`, y además faltan `layer`, `percentage` y `reason`; `quantity` tampoco coincide con `discountedQty`.

observations.content:

observations.title: Verified AppliedDiscount create failure source
observations.content:
**What**: Verified that `tx.appliedDiscount.create()` in `stock-controll-back` fails because `AppliedDiscount.type` is required in Prisma while `normalizeAppliedDiscount()` passes `rule.type` as `null` for universal discount rules; `orderId` and `discountRuleId` remain valid through Prisma's `UncheckedCreateInput`.
**Why**: The user asked to isolate whether the create failure was caused by `type: null`, scalar foreign keys instead of `connect`, or both.
**Where**: `stock-controll-back/prisma/schema.prisma`, `stock-controll-back/services/salesServices.js`, `stock-controll-back/node_modules/.prisma/client/index.d.ts`
**Learned**: Prisma 6.19 generates `data: XOR<AppliedDiscountCreateInput, AppliedDiscountUncheckedCreateInput>` for this model. The unchecked branch accepts `orderId` and `discountRuleId`, but still requires non-null `type`, so a null enum value invalidates that branch and Prisma surfaces relation-field hints from the checked branch.

observations.title: Recommended nullable AppliedDiscount type
observations.content:
**What**: Analicé la incompatibilidad entre `DiscountRule.type` nullable para reglas universales y `AppliedDiscount.type` obligatorio, y recomendé volver nullable `AppliedDiscount.type` en lugar de derivarlo heurísticamente desde `conditionsUniversal`.
**Why**: Las reglas universales son componibles; mapearlas a un enum legacy cerrado (`DiscountType`) puede producir auditoría falsa y romper ventas al persistir descuentos cuando `rule.type` es null.
**Where**: `stock-controll-back/prisma/schema.prisma`, `stock-controll-back/services/salesServices.js`, `stock-controll-back/openspec/changes/universal-discount-rules/spec.md`
**Learned**: El schema ya hizo nullable `DiscountRule.type` y `layer`, pero `AppliedDiscount.type` sigue requerido; `normalizeAppliedDiscount()` copia `rule.type` tal cual, por lo que una venta con regla universal puede fallar dentro de la transacción al insertar auditoría.

observations.content:
## Goal
Diagnose the exact Prisma validation failure in `stock-controll-back` for `tx.appliedDiscount.create()` and determine whether it was caused by `type: null`, scalar foreign keys, or both.

## Instructions
- Investigate precisely before concluding.
- Return root cause and the minimum correct fix with an exact valid `data` example.

## Discoveries
- `DiscountRule.type` is nullable by design for `engineVersion: 'universal'` rules in `prisma/schema.prisma`.
- `AppliedDiscount.type` is still required in the Prisma schema, creating a domain mismatch for audit rows derived from universal rules.
- Prisma 6.19 generates `data: XOR<AppliedDiscountCreateInput, AppliedDiscountUncheckedCreateInput>` for `appliedDiscount.create()`.
- `AppliedDiscountUncheckedCreateInput` explicitly allows `orderId` and `discountRuleId`, so scalar foreign keys are valid in `create()` for this model.
- `normalizeAppliedDiscount()` in `services/salesServices.js` intentionally propagates `rule.type` as `null` for universal rules, which invalidates the unchecked branch and leads Prisma to surface checked-input relation hints.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Read `prisma/schema.prisma` and confirmed `AppliedDiscount.type` is non-null while `DiscountRule.type` is nullable.
- ✅ Read `services/salesServices.js` and found the exact logic that passes `type: rule.type` and comments that it can be `null`.
- ✅ Verified in generated Prisma client types that `orderId` and `discountRuleId` are accepted by `AppliedDiscountUncheckedCreateInput`.
- ✅ Determined the precise root cause: `type: null`, not the use of scalar foreign keys.

## Next Steps
- If requested, apply the minimal fix by making `AppliedDiscount.type` nullable and creating the corresponding Prisma migration.
- Optionally document that using `connect` is stylistic here, not required for correctness.

## Relevant Files
- `stock-controll-back/prisma/schema.prisma` — defines `DiscountRule` and `AppliedDiscount` nullability mismatch.
- `stock-controll-back/services/salesServices.js` — normalizes applied discounts before `tx.appliedDiscount.create()`.
- `stock-controll-back/node_modules/.prisma/client/index.d.ts` — generated Prisma types proving scalar FK support in unchecked create.

observations.title: Fixed hook order crash in SaleDetail
observations.content:
**What**: Movi el guard clause de `SaleDetail` para que `useCallback` y `useEffect` siempre se ejecuten antes del `return null`, y ajusté el `useEffect` para activarse solo cuando `isOpen` y `saleData` existen.
**Why**: React estaba lanzando `Rendered more hooks than during the previous render` después de una venta exitosa porque `SaleDetail` primero renderizaba sin hooks (`currentSale === null`) y luego con hooks cuando `NewSale` seteaba la venta confirmada.
**Where**: `stock-controll/src/pages/sales/SaleDetail.jsx`, llamado desde `stock-controll/src/pages/sales/NewSale.jsx`.
**Learned**: El cambio reciente en `NewSale` que abre `SaleDetail` al pasar `currentSale` de `null` a objeto expone inmediatamente cualquier hook declarado después de un early return en el modal.

# Proposal: Agregar Tests con Vitest

## Intent

Agregar cobertura de tests básica al proyecto test-sdd-counter utilizando Vitest. El proyecto actualmente no tiene tests y se necesita verificar el comportamiento del contador (incremento, decremento, reset).

## Scope

### In Scope
- Agregar Vitest como devDependency
- Crear archivo de tests `counter.test.js`
- Tests para: incremento (+1), decremento (-1), reset (volver a 0)
- Configurar script de test en package.json
- Extraer lógica del contador a módulo separado para facilitar testing

### Out of Scope
- Refactorizar la UI o estilos
- Tests de integración con DOM
- Coverage avanzado o reporting fancy

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `test-coverage`: Tests unitarios básicos para la lógica del contador

## Approach

1. Instalar Vitest: `npm install -D vitest`
2. Extraer la lógica del contador a `counter.js` (separar presentación de lógica)
3. Crear `tests/counter.test.js` con tests para las tres operaciones
4. Actualizar `package.json` con script de test
5. Modificar `index.html` para importar el módulo

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `package.json` | Modified | Agregar vitest y script de test |
| `counter.js` | New | Lógica del contador separada |
| `tests/counter.test.js` | New | Archivo de tests |
| `index.html` | Modified | Importar counter.js en lugar de lógica embebida |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Tests rompen por separada lógica | Low | Tests simples, lógica trivial |

## Rollback Plan

1. Eliminar `vitest` de devDependencies
2. Eliminar `counter.js` y `tests/`
3. Volver la lógica del contador inline en `index.html`
4. Eliminar script de test en package.json

observations.title: Design agregar-tests-vitest
observations.content:
# Design: Agregar Tests con Vitest

## Technical Approach

Agregar Vitest al proyecto vanilla test-sdd-counter y refactorizar la lógica del contador para que sea testable unitariamente. El enfoque será extraer la lógica de negocio a un módulo JS separado, permitiendo testing directo de las funciones increment, decrement y reset.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: Estructura de archivos de tests

**Choice**: tests/ counter.test.js
**Alternatives considered**: tests/unit/counter.spec.js (naming inconsistency con otros proyectos del workspace)
**Rationale**: counter.test.js sigue convención Vitest default y es consistente con el estándar de la industria.

### Decision: Refactorización para testabilidad

**Choice**: Extraer lógica del contador a src/counter.js
**Alternatives considered**: Testing directo del DOM (jsdom), Testing del comportamiento via console.log mocking
**Rationale**: Extraer la lógica a un módulo permite tests unitarios puros sin dependencia del browser. El archivo HTML simplemente importa el módulo y llama a init().

## Data Flow

    index.html
         │
         ▼ (importa e inicializa)
    src/counter.js
         │
         ├── count.js (lógica pura: increment, decrement, reset)
         │
    tests/
         └── counter.test.js (tests unitarios de count.js)

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `package.json` | Modify | Agregar vitest como devDependency y script test |
| `vite.config.js` | Create | Configuración de Vitest para proyecto vanilla |
| `src/counter.js` | Create | Módulo con lógica del contador (count + init) |
| `src/count.js` | Create | Lógica pura del contador (increment, decrement, reset) |
| `tests/counter.test.js` | Create | Tests unitarios para count.js |
| `index.html` | Modify | Importar src/counter.js en lugar de lógica inline |

## Interfaces / Contracts

```javascript
// src/count.js - lógica pura
export function increment(count) { return count + 1; }
export function decrement(count) { return count - 1; }
export function reset() { return 0; }
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Unit | Funciones increment, decrement, reset | Tests directos con assert.strictEqual |
| Integration | Contador completo con DOM | Ninguno (proyecto simple, suficiente con unit) |

## Migration / Rollout

No migration required.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Ninguno - el enfoque es directo

observations.title: Spec agregar-tests-contador
observations.content:
# Contador Tests Specification

## Purpose

Verificar el comportamiento correcto de las funciones del contador mediante tests unitarios.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Increment

El contador debe incremento su valor en 1 cada vez que se llama a la función increment().

#### Scenario: Incremento básico

- GIVEN un contador con valor 0
- WHEN se llama a increment()
- THEN el valor del contador debe ser 1

#### Scenario: Múltiples incrementos

- GIVEN un contador con valor 5
- WHEN se llama a increment() tres veces
- THEN el valor del contador debe ser 8

### Requirement: Decrement

El contador debe decrementar su valor en 1 cada vez que se llama a la función decrement().

#### Scenario: Decremento básico

- GIVEN un contador con valor 0
- WHEN se llama a decrement()
- THEN el valor del contador debe ser -1

#### Scenario: Múltiples decrementos

- GIVEN un contador con valor 3
- WHEN se llama a decrement() dos veces
- THEN el valor del contador debe ser 1

### Requirement: Reset

El contador debe restablecer su valor a 0 cada vez que se llama a la función reset().

#### Scenario: Reset básico

- GIVEN un contador con valor 5
- WHEN se llama a reset()
- THEN el valor del contador debe ser 0

#### Scenario: Reset después de múltiples operaciones

- GIVEN un contador con valor -3
- WHEN se llama a increment() dos veces y luego reset()
- THEN el valor del contador debe ser 0

# Proposal: Excel Export for All Sections

## Goal
Implement Excel download functionality (`.xlsx`) for all key reporting and management sections of the application.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The exports will be implemented as dedicated GET endpoints to ensure proper binary streaming and high performance.
> Every section (Sales, Products, Movements, etc.) will have a button/route to trigger its specific download.

## Proposed Sections
1. **Sales**: Detailed history of orders.
2. **Products**: Current inventory and pricing.
3. **Seller Performance**: Aggregated statistics by employee.
4. **Stock History**: Traceability of entries and exits.
5. **Movements**: Registered cash/inventory movements.
6. **Clients/Suppliers**: Basic contact data and balance.

## Approach
- **Infrastructure**: Install `exceljs`.
- **Core**: Create `services/excelExportService.js` to handle workbook creation and styling.
- **Routes**: Add `/api/reports/export/[section]` or append `export` action to existing routes.
- **Authentication**: Reuse existing RBAC checks.

## Risks
- **Date Range Filters**: Need to ensure the Excel export respects the same filters (from/to) as the UI.
- **Large Data**: Use ExcelJS `stream` mode for very large datasets to prevent memory exhaustion.

observations.title: sdd/stock-controll-back-main/explore/prisma-error-stock-history
observations.content:
## Exploration: Prisma Error in stockHistory.create()

**Topic**: Invalid invocation of `prisma.stockHistory.create()` when creating a new product.

**Findings**:
- The error occurs in `services/productsServices.js` within the `create` function (lines 73-84).
- The `create` call for `stockHistory` uses a mixed approach: `store` is using `connect` (checked write), while `productId` is used as a scalar (unchecked write).
- Other successful calls to `stockHistory.create()` (e.g., in `salesServices.js` and `adjustStock` in `productsServices.js`) use `storeId` directly as a scalar.
- Prisma validation fails when these styles are mixed or when the specific model doesn't handle the combination as expected.
- Since the product is already created and its ID is available (`response.id`), using `storeId` instead of `store: { connect: ... }` is the safest and most consistent fix.

**Proposed Solution**:
Change `store: { connect: { id: user.storeId } }` to `storeId: user.storeId` in `services/productsServices.js:75`.

**Tradeoffs**:
- Using `storeId` is an "unchecked" write, which skips some Prisma-level validation (like checking if the store exists), but since `user.storeId` comes from the authenticated user context and was just used to create the product, it's guaranteed to be valid.
- This maintains consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**Relevant Files**:
- `services/productsServices.js`

observations.title: Fix Prisma mixed relations en productsServices.js
observations.content:
**What**: Corregidas las 3 llamadas a `prisma.stockHistory.create()` en productsServices.js.
**Why**: Mezclaban el estilo relacional (`store: { connect: ... }`) con campos escalares (`productId`, `userId`), causando el error "Invalid prisma.stockHistory.create() invocation: product is required".
**Where**: `services/productsServices.js` — funciones `create` (línea 73), `update` (línea 224), `adjustStock` (línea 292).
**Learned**: Prisma no permite mezclar `ModelCreateInput` (relational) con `ModelUncheckedCreateInput` (scalar) en el mismo objeto `data`. Todos los demás servicios (suppliers, clients, categories, caja, movimientos, discounts) ya usaban el estilo relacional correcto. El patrón para campos opcionales es `user: id ? { connect: { id } } : undefined`.

observations.content:
# Proposal: Anular Ventas (Updated)

## Intent
Implement a robust mechanism to void/cancel sales that were performed incorrectly. This ensures stock integrity, accounting accuracy, and provides an audit trail for corrections.

## Scope
- Backend: `PATCH /api/sales/:id/cancel` endpoint with stock reversal and **password verification**.
- Backend: Enforce `sale.cancel` permission.
- Frontend: "Anular Venta" button in `SaleDetail.jsx` with **password re-entry requirement**.

## Approach
Status Update to `CANCELLED` + Stock Reversal in transaction + Mandatory Password Check.

## Success Criteria
- Stock is correctly incremented.
- StockHistory shows `RETURN`.
- Permissions enforced.
- Operation fails if password is wrong.

observations.title: sdd/anular-ventas/spec
observations.content:
# Sale Cancellation Specification

## Requirements
- **Void Sale Authorization**: MUST have `sale.cancel` permission AND verify password.
- **Stock Reversal**: MUST return items to inventory and record `RETURN` in StockHistory.
- **Transactional Integrity**: MUST be atomic.

## Scenarios
- Happy path: Correct password -> Cancelled + Stock restored.
- Error path: Wrong password -> 401 error.
- Error path: No permission -> 403 error.
- Error path: DB failure -> Rollback.

observations.title: sdd/anular-ventas/design
observations.content:

Transactional status update to `CANCELLED` + stock reversal + password check.

- **Stock Reversal**: Direct `increment` inside the transaction.

- `backend/services/salesServices.js`
- `frontend/src/pages/sales/SaleDetail.jsx`

observations.title: sdd/cuentas-corrientes/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Cuentas Corrientes

## Intent
Implement a system for client debt management, partial payments in sales, and dedicated payment processing.

## Scope
- Models: CurrentAccount, CurrentAccountMovement.
- Sales: Partial payments supported if CC method is used.
- Module: Open/Close accounts, Register payments, View history.

## Approach
Integrated Debt Management using dedicated tables and Prisma transactions for balance integrity.

## Risks
Concurrency on balance updates. Strict validation for client type.

observations.title: sdd/cuentas-corrientes/spec
observations.content:
# Cuentas Corrientes Specification

## Requirements
- **Account Management**: Encargado/Admin/Sistema can open. Only Admin/Sistema can close if balance=0.
- **Sales Integration**: "Cuenta Corriente" method only for valid clients with open accounts. Supports partial payments.
- **Debt Payment**: Decrease balance, log movement, and register INCOME in CashRegister.
- **Visualization**: Detailed audit log of movements with balance tracking.

## Scenarios
- Partial payment: Total $5k, Paid $2k -> $3k debt added.
- Payment: $2k payment -> Balance decreases, CashRegister INCOME logged.
- Security: Forbidden for "Consumidor Final".

observations.title: sdd/cuentas-corrientes/design
observations.content:
# Design: Cuentas Corrientes

## Tech Decisions
- Atomic updates for balance using Prisma $transaction.
- Detailed movement log storing total, paid, and debt per operation.
- Payments to CC must link to CashRegister INCOME.

## Models
- CurrentAccount (status, balance, storeId).
- CurrentAccountMovement (type, amounts, balanceResult).

## Flow
- NewSale -> detect CC method -> calculate debt -> update balance + log movement.
- Register Payment -> decrease balance -> log movement + CashMovement income.

observations.content:
## Goal
Configurar el proyecto para correr localmente tanto el frontend como el backend.

## Instructions
- Se configuró el frontend para apuntar al backend local (http://localhost:3000).
- Se detectó que la conexión al pooler de Supabase (puerto 6543) falla en este entorno, por lo que se validó y recomendó usar DIRECT_URL (puerto 5432).

## Discoveries
- El pooler de Supabase (6543) no responde en el entorno local, pero la conexión directa (5432) funciona perfectamente.
- El frontend no tenía `.env` ni `node_modules` inicializados.
- Existe un usuario `maxi@maxi.com` en la base de datos de prueba.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Inicialización de SDD (sdd-init) para ambos repositorios.
- ✅ Instalación de dependencias (`npm install`) en frontend y backend.
- ✅ Generación de Prisma Client en el backend.
- ✅ Creación de archivo `.env` en el frontend con `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000`.
- ✅ Validación de conexión a base de datos remota.

## Next Steps
- El usuario debe ejecutar `npm run dev` en ambas terminales para comenzar las pruebas.

## Relevant Files
- `stock-controll-back/.env` — Configuración de base de datos y secretos.
- `stock-controll-main/.env` — Nueva configuración para apuntar al API local.
- `stock-controll-back/check_db.js` — Script modificado para usar DIRECT_URL en pruebas de conexión.

- ✅ Registro de Service Worker en `index.html`.
- ✅ Lógica de captura de prompt en `main.jsx`.

observations.title: Descuentos Parciales y Validación Flexible
observations.content:
**What**: Implementación de descuentos parciales proporcionales y flexibilización de validación de pagos.
**Why**: Permitir descuentos que solo apliquen sobre la porción del pago correspondiente al medio elegido, y evitar errores 401 por discrepancias menores o vueltos.
**Where**: salesServices.js, evaluator.js, calculator.js, schema.prisma, DiscountFormModal.jsx.
**Learned**: Windows bloquea node_modules durante prisma generate si el server está activo. La validación de pagos debe ser de suficiencia (>=) no de igualdad estricta (==) para soportar vueltos.

observations.title: Session summary: stock-controll-back
observations.content:
## Goal
Refactorizar la lógica de pagos y descuentos para soportar pagos combinados y descuentos proporcionales.

## Instructions
- El frontend no debe hacer cálculos de precios.
- El backend debe aceptar sobre-pagos (vueltos).

## Discoveries
- El error 401 ocurría porque la validación de pagos exigía igualdad estricta, lo cual fallaba al aplicar descuentos calculados solo en el back.
- Windows bloquea los archivos de Prisma si el servidor de desarrollo está corriendo durante un `prisma generate`.

## Accomplished
- ✅ DB: Agregado campo `allowPartial` a `DiscountRule`.
- ✅ Engine: Refactorizado `evaluator.js` y `calculator.js` para manejar `matchingAmount`.
- ✅ Backend: Flexibilizada la función `validatePayments` en `salesServices.js`.
- ✅ Frontend: Agregado checkbox "Permitir en pagos parciales" en el formulario de descuentos.

## Relevant Files
- `services/salesServices.js` — Validación de pagos y creación de venta.
- `services/discountEngine/universal/evaluator.js` — Lógica de matching de montos de pago.
- `services/discountEngine/universal/calculator.js` — Cálculo proporcional de porcentajes.
- `src/components/Discounts/UniversalRuleBuilder.jsx` — UI del checkbox parcial.

observations.title: Fix Descuentos Parciales en Simulador
observations.content:
**What**: Corrección de bug en descuentos parciales donde se ignoraba el monto proporcional en el simulador.
**Why**: La función preview no extraía paymentBreakdown del body y mergeEngineResults perdía el flag allowPartial durante el enriquecimiento.
**Where**: discountService.js, NewSale.jsx.
**Learned**: Siempre verificar que todas las capas (Controller -> Service -> Engine -> Merger) preserven los metadatos necesarios para el cálculo cascada.

observations.title: Fix Validación Cuenta Corriente con Descuentos
observations.content:
**What**: Corrección de validación estricta en ventas con Cuenta Corriente y normalización de nombres de medios de pago.
**Why**: Las ventas con CC fallaban cuando se aplicaban descuentos parciales porque la validación comparaba montos brutos contra netos usando igualdad estricta.
**Where**: salesServices.js, discountService.js.
**Learned**: La normalización de inputs debe ocurrir lo más temprano posible y ser consistente en todos los servicios (Sale vs Discount Preview). Las validaciones de pago deben ser siempre de suficiencia (>=) para evitar falsos negativos por descuentos o vueltos.

observations.title: Session summary: stock-controll-back
observations.content:
## Goal
Finalizar la implementación de descuentos parciales proporcionales y resolver errores de validación en ventas mixtas (Efectivo + Cuenta Corriente).

## Instructions
- Se estableció que la validación de pagos debe ser por suficiencia (`totalPaid >= computedTotal`).
- Se debe normalizar siempre "Cuenta Corriente" a "CUENTA_CORRIENTE" antes de procesar descuentos o ventas.

## Discoveries
- El motor universal no recibía `paymentBreakdown` en el preview, causando que los descuentos parciales se aplicaran sobre el total.
- La validación de Cuenta Corriente en `salesServices.js` era estricta e ignoraba la flexibilización aplicada a las ventas normales.
- Existe una discrepancia de nombres entre el Frontend (Title Case) y el Backend (Screaming Snake Case) para los medios de pago.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Frontend: `NewSale.jsx` ahora envía el desglose de pagos en el preview de descuentos.
- ✅ Backend: `discountService.js` normaliza medios de pago y extrae montos para el motor.
- ✅ Backend: `salesServices.js` flexibiliza la validación de pagos en ventas con Cuenta Corriente.
- ✅ Backend: `mergeEngineResults` preserva metadatos de descuentos parciales.

## Next Steps
- Monitorear si el usuario requiere agregar "Cuenta Corriente" como opción elegible en el creador de reglas (UniversalRuleBuilder).

**Where**: NewSale.jsx, DiscountSummaryModal.jsx.
**Learned**: Los descuentos proporcionales dependen del medio de pago, lo que requiere un ciclo de retroalimentación en tiempo real dentro del modal.

observations.title: Planning Completed: Reactive Sale Flow

**Why**: Unificar la UX de pagos y descuentos.

observations.title: Reactive Sale Flow refactor completed
observations.content:
**What**: Refactorización completa del flujo de pagos en NewSale — el editor de pagos migró al DiscountSummaryModal.
**Why**: El vendedor necesitaba configurar pagos antes de ver el total con descuentos, lo cual era anti-intuitivo.
**Where**: NewSale.jsx (limpieza de estado y UI), DiscountSummaryModal.jsx (nuevo editor de pagos con debounce 300ms).
**Learned**: El modal tiene estado local `localBreakdown` que notifica al padre via `onPaymentChange`. El padre ejecuta `fetchDiscountPreviewWithParams(preferred, excluded, breakdown)`. La función ahora toma el breakdown como parámetro en vez de leerlo del estado global.

**Where**: NewSale.jsx.
**Learned**: Siempre verificar el footer mobile y modales secundarios al eliminar variables de estado core de un componente grande. Re-definí netTotal para mantener la UI reactiva sin depender del estado de pagos interno de NewSale.

observations.title: Session summary: stock-controll-main
observations.content:
## Goal
Refactorizar el flujo de venta POS para centralizar la configuración de pagos y descuentos en un único modal reactivo ("Estación de Cierre").

## Discoveries
- Delegar la lógica de pagos al modal simplifica enormemente el componente NewSale.jsx.
- Se requiere un debounce (300ms) al notificar cambios de pagos desde el modal para evitar saturar el endpoint de /api/discounts/preview.
- El modal debe gestionar su propio estado de "Monto Restante" y validar la cobertura total antes de permitir finalizar la venta.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Refactorización completa de DiscountSummaryModal.jsx convirtiéndolo en el controlador principal del cierre.
- ✅ Limpieza de NewSale.jsx: eliminación de estados redundantes de pagos y actualización del sidebar.
- ✅ Implementación de reactividad entre selección de pagos y cálculo de descuentos.
- ✅ Fix de ReferenceError (showCashCalculator, netTotal) tras la limpieza de lógica.

## Next Steps
- Realizar pruebas de estrés con múltiples medios de pago y descuentos cruzados.
- Validar el comportamiento en móviles del nuevo flujo de cierre.

## Relevant Files
- src/pages/sales/NewSale.jsx — Limpieza de lógica y UI simplificada.
- src/components/Modals/DiscountSummaryModal.jsx — Nueva lógica de estación de cierre y editor de pagos.

observations.content:

**Why**: Prisma no permite valores nulos en campos requeridos dentro de un objeto `where`.

observations.title: Fixed cash calculation in split payments and closure
observations.content:
**What**: Se unificó la lógica de cálculo de efectivo en el cierre de caja y el historial de actividad, y se implementó normalización de nombres de medios de pago.
**Why**: Las ventas combinadas (Efectivo + CC) no sumaban el efectivo al arqueo de caja debido a una validación de string demasiado estricta en el cierre.
**Where**: backend/services/cajaServices.js, backend/services/salesServices.js
**Learned**: En sistemas con múltiples medios de pago, es más seguro usar una lógica de exclusión (todo lo que no sea digital es efectivo) que una de inclusión estricta.

observations.title: Fixed Cash Register Closing Calculation for Split Payments
observations.content:
**What**: Se unificó la lógica de cálculo de efectivo esperado en el cierre de caja para contemplar ventas combinadas.
**Why**: El modal de cierre ignoraba pagos en efectivo dentro de ventas combinadas si el método de pago de la orden principal era 'COMBINADO', causando falsos excedentes.
**Where**: backend/services/cajaServices.js
**Learned**: Los cálculos de arqueo deben iterar siempre sobre el desglose de pagos (OrderPayment) y no confiar solo en el método principal de la orden.

observations.title: Fix Conciliación Caja y Discrepancia Descuentos Backend/Frontend
observations.content:
**What**: Corregida conciliación de caja para pagos combinados y detectada falla en base de cálculo de descuentos del backend.
**Why**: Las ventas mixtas (Efectivo + CC) no cuadraban en la caja física.
**Where**: src/pages/sales/CashRegister.jsx, services/salesServices.js, services/discountEngine/universal/calculator.js
**Learned**: El backend aplica descuentos de pago sobre el monto neto pagado en lugar del subtotal bruto cuando allowPartial es true, causando discrepancias con el frontend. Se corrigió la persistencia de amoutPayed para usar el pago real recibido.

observations.content:
# Proposal: add-vitest

## Intent

No test runner exists in the project — this blocks TDD and makes refactoring risky. Add Vitest as the test framework to enable test-driven development with fast feedback and built-in coverage support.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Install `vitest` and `@vitejs/plugin-react` (Vitest provider for Vite)
- Configure `vite.config.js` with Vitest settings
- Create one example passing test to validate the setup

### Out of Scope
- Feature tests (no component tests yet)
- CI/CD integration
- Coverage thresholds
- Additional test utilities (e.g., `@testing-library/react`)

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `vitest-test-runner`: Installed and configured test runner with React plugin support

### Modified Capabilities
- None

## Approach

1. Install `vitest` and `@vitejs/plugin-react` as dev dependencies
2. Update `vite.config.js` to add Vitest configuration with `test: { globals: true, environment: 'jsdom' }`
3. Add `test` script to `package.json`
4. Create `src/test/example.test.js` with a simple passing test (e.g., `expect(1 + 1).toBe(2)`)
5. Verify `pnpm test` runs successfully

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `package.json` | Modified | Add `vitest`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `jsdom` deps; add `test` script |
| `vite.config.js` | Modified | Add Vitest plugin and test configuration |
| `src/test/` | New | Example test file directory |
| `src/test/example.test.js` | New | First passing test |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Version conflict with Vite 8 | Low | Pin compatible Vitest version (~3.x matches Vite 8) |
| JSdom environment missing | Low | Install `jsdom` explicitly if `pnpm test` fails |

## Rollback Plan

```bash
pnpm remove vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom
# Revert vite.config.js to previous state
git checkout vite.config.js
```

## Dependencies

- None (Vitest ~3.x is compatible with Vite 8)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `pnpm test` runs without errors
- [ ] At least 1 test passes
- [ ] No warnings about missing peer dependencies

# Landing Design Tokens Specification

## Purpose

CSS custom properties and Tailwind theme tokens for the premium lawyer landing page aesthetic: dark navy + gold palette, Playfair Display + Inter typography, and subtle glassmorphism.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Navy Color Palette

The system SHALL provide custom Tailwind color utilities for the navy palette.

#### Scenario: Navy-900 in utility classes

- GIVEN a React component using `className="bg-navy-900 text-white"`
- WHEN the component renders
- THEN the background SHALL be #0F172A (dark navy)
- AND text SHALL render as white

#### Scenario: Navy-800 for secondary surfaces

- GIVEN `className="bg-navy-800"`
- WHEN rendered
- THEN the background SHALL be #1E3A8A (navy deep)

### Requirement: Gold Accent Colors

The system SHALL provide gold/amber accent colors for CTAs and highlights.

#### Scenario: Gold-amber for primary actions

- GIVEN `className="bg-gold-amber text-white"`
- WHEN rendered
- THEN the background SHALL be #B45309 (amber gold)

#### Scenario: Gold-accent for decorative borders

- GIVEN `className="border border-gold-accent"`
- WHEN rendered
- THEN the border SHALL be #CA8A04

### Requirement: Typography System

The system SHALL provide Playfair Display for headings and Inter for body text via Google Fonts.

#### Scenario: Heading font loaded

- GIVEN Google Fonts loaded via index.html preconnect
- WHEN browser fetches fonts
- THEN Playfair Display SHALL be available for headings
- AND Inter SHALL be available for body text

### Requirement: Glassmorphism Utilities

The system SHALL provide subtle glassmorphism utility classes.

#### Scenario: Glass card with backdrop blur

- GIVEN `className="bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-md border border-white/10"`
- WHEN rendered
- THEN the element SHALL have ~12px backdrop blur
- AND translucent white background at 10% opacity
- AND subtle white border at 10% opacity

### Requirement: CSS Custom Properties

The system SHALL expose CSS custom properties for programmatic access.

#### Scenario: CSS variable access

- GIVEN `style={{ color: 'var(--color-navy-900)' }}`
- WHEN applied to an element
- THEN the color SHALL be #0F172A

## Design Tokens Reference

| Token | Hex | Usage |
|-------|-----|-------|
| --color-navy-900 | #0F172A | Primary background |
| --color-navy-800 | #1E3A8A | Secondary surfaces |
| --color-navy-700 | #1E40AF | Tertiary elements |
| --color-gold-amber | #B45309 | Primary CTAs |
| --color-gold-accent | #CA8A04 | Decorative/borders |
| --font-heading | 'Playfair Display', serif | Headings |
| --font-body | 'Inter', sans-serif | Body text |

observations.content:
# Design: landing-aesthetics-foundation

## Technical Approach

Establish the visual foundation for the landing page: Google Fonts integration and Tailwind CSS v4 theme tokens (navy palette, gold accents, Playfair Display + Inter fonts) via the CSS-first `@theme` directive. No component logic or data flow — pure CSS configuration that components will consume via `className`.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: CSS-first theme configuration

**Choice**: Define all design tokens in `src/index.css` using Tailwind v4's `@theme` directive
**Alternatives considered**: `tailwind.config.js` (doesn't exist in v4 — deprecated), separate CSS token file (unnecessary indirection)
**Rationale**: Tailwind v4's `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin processes CSS directly. Co-locating tokens with the import keeps the setup simple and leverages Tailwind's built-in purging.

### Decision: Google Fonts loading strategy

**Choice**: `<link rel="preconnect">` in `index.html` + `@import` in CSS for font files
**Alternatives considered**: CSS-only `@import` without preconnect (slower first paint), `<link>` tags only without CSS import (duplication)
**Rationale**: Preconnect establishes early DNS/TCP/TLS handshake. The CSS `@import` ensures fonts are in the CSS bundle and cached properly.

### Decision: Glassmorphism via Tailwind arbitrary values

**Choice**: Use Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax (`bg-white/10`, `backdrop-blur-[12px]`) for glassmorphism
**Alternatives considered**: Custom CSS class for every glass variant (proliferation), only standard Tailwind glass classes (insufficient subtlety)
**Rationale**: Tailwind v4 arbitrary values provide the exact translucency needed without creating maintenance-heavy custom classes.

## Data Flow

No data flow — pure CSS configuration:

1. Tokens defined in CSS as custom properties inside `@theme`
2. Compiled by Tailwind v4 into utility classes
3. Consumed by React components via `className`

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `index.html` | Modify | Add Google Fonts preconnect links, fix `<title>`, set `lang="es"` |
| `src/index.css` | Modify | Add `@theme` with color/typography tokens, Google Fonts `@import`, base styles |

## Interface Contracts

### Tailwind Theme Tokens (generated from @theme)

```
Colors:
  navy-900  → #0F172A   (--color-navy-900)
  navy-800  → #1E3A8A   (--color-navy-800)
  navy-700  → #1E40AF   (--color-navy-700)
  gold-amber → #B45309  (--color-gold-amber)
  gold-accent → #CA8A04 (--color-gold-accent)

Fonts:
  heading → 'Playfair Display', serif
  body → 'Inter', sans-serif
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Build | CSS compiles without errors | `pnpm build` succeeds |
| Visual | Tokens resolve to correct values | Browser devtools inspection |
| Regression | Existing styles unaffected | Compare before/after build output |

## Migration / Rollout

No migration required. This is an additive change only — new CSS tokens that don't affect existing styles.

## Open Questions

None — all technical decisions are resolved.

observations.title: CSS Architecture Exploration - Tailwind v4 Refactor Analysis
observations.content:
**What**: Comprehensive analysis of the lawyer portfolio's CSS architecture, identifying massive duplication between custom CSS utilities and Tailwind v4's generated utilities.

**Why**: To plan a refactor that uses Tailwind v4 properly without losing the premium visual aesthetics the client values.

**Where**: 
- `src/index.css` — entry point
- `src/styles/tokens.css` — design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, shadows)
- `src/styles/base.css` — CSS reset + ~150 duplicated utility classes
- `src/styles/utilities.css` — premium custom utilities (gold effects, glassmorphism, cards, buttons, animations)
- `vite.config.js` — @tailwindcss/vite plugin
- All JSX components in `src/components/`

**Learned**:
- Tailwind v4 is imported LAST in index.css (`@import "tailwindcss"` after custom CSS files). This means Tailwind's generated utilities override custom ones with identical names. Much of `base.css` is effectively dead code.
- `base.css` manually reimplements standard Tailwind utilities: `.flex`, `.grid`, `.gap-*`, `.p-*`, `.m-*`, `.rounded`, `.shadow-*`, `.transition-*`, `.hidden`, `.block`, `.w-*`, `.h-*`, responsive variants like `.md\:flex`, etc.
- The custom semantic classes (`.text-primary`, `.bg-surface`, `.nav-link`, `.btn-primary`, `.gold-divider`) are valuable and unique — these define the brand identity.
- Visual identity pillars: Gold gradient accents (`#B45309` to `#CA8A04`), deep navy (`#0F172A`), cream palette (`#FAFAF9`), Cormorant serif + Montserrat sans-serif, glassmorphism cards, gold shimmer hover effect, elegant scrollbar/selection styling.
- Dark mode is implemented via CSS custom properties scoped to `.dark` class on `<html>`, toggled with localStorage persistence.
- Tailwind v4's CSS-first configuration (@theme, @utility, @layer) is the right path for preserving custom design tokens while eliminating redundancy.

observations.title: sdd/css-tailwind-v4-refactor/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: css-tailwind-v4-refactor

## Intent
Refactor CSS architecture to proper Tailwind v4 CSS-first architecture. Current setup has 500+ lines of duplicated utilities in base.css that conflict with Tailwind v4's `@import "tailwindcss"` (imported last, overriding custom tokens). Goal: migrate to `@theme` and `@utility` directives while preserving ALL premium visual aesthetics.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Migrate design tokens from `:root` CSS custom properties to Tailwind v4 `@theme` block
- Create `@utility` definitions for semantic classes (bg-surface, text-primary, max-w-container-max, etc.)
- Migrate premium effects from utilities.css to `@layer utilities` 
- Remove duplicated Tailwind utilities from base.css (keep only reset + typography base)
- Fix import order in index.css so Tailwind doesn't override custom values
- Preserve: gold gradient text, glassmorphism, card hover effects, button system, nav underline animation, gold shimmer, custom scrollbar, dark mode

### Out of Scope
- Changing any component JSX or logic
- Changing the color palette or typography choices
- Adding new visual effects

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `tailwind-v4-theme`: Proper Tailwind v4 `@theme` block with all design tokens
- `tailwind-v4-utilities`: Semantic utility definitions via `@utility` directive
- `css-architecture-cleanup`: Consolidated architecture with no duplication

### Modified Capabilities
- None (pure refactor, CSS architecture only)

## Approach
1. Consolidate tokens.css + base.css into single `@theme` block in index.css
2. Define semantic utilities using `@utility` for App.jsx compatibility
3. Migrate premium effects from utilities.css to `@layer utilities`
4. Remove duplicated utilities from base.css (lines 186-1033)
5. Ensure proper import order: fonts → tokens → base → utilities → tailwindcss

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/index.css` | Modified | Main entry, will host @theme block |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/tokens.css` | Removed | Merged into @theme |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/base.css` | Modified | Remove duplicated utilities, keep reset |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/utilities.css` | Modified | Migrate to @layer utilities |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Visual regression | Medium | Comprehensive before/after comparison in verify phase |
| Tailwind v4 theme syntax errors | Low | Follow official Tailwind v4 docs for @theme |
| Breaking App.jsx class references | Medium | Audit all className usages before removing |

## Rollback Plan
1. Revert index.css, tokens.css, base.css, utilities.css to pre-change state via git
2. All changes are in CSS only — no JSX impact
3. Git revert: `git checkout HEAD -- lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/ lawyerPortfolio/src/index.css`

## Dependencies
- Tailwind CSS v4 documentation for @theme/@utility syntax
- Audit of all className usages in JSX files

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All design tokens work in both light and dark mode
- [ ] No visual differences in hero, services, contact, or any section
- [ ] Dark mode toggle functions correctly
- [ ] All responsive breakpoints work
- [ ] Custom shadows and radii render correctly
- [ ] Build succeeds with no CSS errors

observations.content:
# Tailwind v4 CSS Architecture Refactor Specification

## Purpose
Refactor CSS architecture to proper Tailwind v4 CSS-first architecture, consolidating design tokens and removing duplicated utilities.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Tailwind v4 Theme Block

The system SHALL define all design tokens in a Tailwind v4 `@theme` block within index.css. This block MUST include: color palette (navy, gold, cream), typography (Cormorant headings, Montserrat body), spacing scale, shadow scale, border-radius scale, and transition timing.

#### Scenario: Light mode theme tokens

- GIVEN user visits portfolio in light mode
- WHEN page loads
- THEN all colors resolve to light theme values (cream background, navy text, gold accents)
- AND shadows render with proper opacity
- AND border-radius uses standard scale values

#### Scenario: Dark mode theme tokens

- GIVEN user has dark mode enabled
- WHEN page loads
- THEN all colors resolve to dark theme values (deep navy background, slate text, same gold accents)
- AND glassmorphism uses dark mode appropriate values

### Requirement: Semantic Utility Classes

The system SHALL define semantic utility classes using `@utility` directive for App.jsx compatibility. These MUST include: `bg-surface`, `text-primary`, `max-w-container-max`, `px-margin-mobile`, `px-margin-desktop`, `font-display-lg`, `font-headline-lg`, `text-display-lg`, `text-headline-lg`.

#### Scenario: Semantic utilities in components

- GIVEN App.jsx uses className="bg-surface text-primary"
- WHEN Tailwind processes CSS
- THEN these classes resolve to proper background and text colors
- AND work in both light and dark modes

### Requirement: Premium Effects Layer

The system SHALL migrate all premium effects from utilities.css to `@layer utilities` in index.css. These MUST include: gold-gradient-text, gold-shimmer, glass-card, glass-card-hover, card, card-elevated, card-accent, btn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-ghost, badge, badge-outline, nav-link, decorative-line, section-divider, animate-fade-in, animate-slide-up, img-elegant.

#### Scenario: Gold gradient text effect

- GIVEN element has className="gold-gradient-text"
- WHEN page renders
- THEN text displays gradient from gold-dark through gold to gold-light
- AND -webkit-text-fill-color is transparent for cross-browser support

#### Scenario: Card hover effect

- GIVEN card element with glass-card-hover class
- WHEN user hovers over card
- THEN background lightens, border becomes gold, shadow expands, element translates up 4px
- AND transition uses ease-out-expo timing

### Requirement: Import Order Integrity

The system SHALL maintain proper CSS import order in index.css: (1) Google Fonts, (2) @theme block with all design tokens, (3) base reset and typography, (4) @layer utilities for premium effects, (5) Tailwind v4 entry point. Tailwind's `@import "tailwindcss"` MUST come AFTER theme definitions to prevent override.

#### Scenario: Custom shadow values render correctly

- GIVEN tokens.css defines --shadow-gold and --shadow-glow
- WHEN page renders elements using these shadows
- THEN shadows display correctly (not overridden by Tailwind defaults)
- AND custom values from tokens.css take precedence

### Requirement: Duplicated Utilities Removal

The system SHALL remove all duplicated Tailwind utility classes from base.css (lines 186-1033). Only reset, typography base, scrollbar, selection, and focus styles SHALL remain. All utility patterns (flex, grid, spacing, border, text, etc.) MUST be removed as they conflict with or duplicate Tailwind's generated utilities.

#### Scenario: No duplicate utilities

- GIVEN base.css no longer contains .flex, .grid, .gap-4, .text-center, etc.
- WHEN Tailwind generates utilities
- THEN no conflicts occur between base.css and Tailwind output
- AND all component className values work correctly with Tailwind

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Light mode displays cream/gold/navy aesthetic correctly
- [ ] Dark mode displays deep navy/gold/slate aesthetic correctly
- [ ] Gold gradient text renders correctly on all supported browsers
- [ ] Glassmorphism cards display proper blur and backdrop effects
- [ ] Button styles (primary, secondary, ghost) render with correct hover states
- [ ] Nav link underline animation triggers on hover
- [ ] Card hover effects work with gold border and shadow transitions
- [ ] All responsive breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop) function correctly
- [ ] Custom scrollbar displays on webkit browsers
- [ ] No CSS conflicts or override warnings in browser devtools

observations.title: sdd/css-architecture-cleanup/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: CSS Architecture Cleanup — Eliminate Redundancy

## Intent

Clean up the CSS architecture to be DRY and leverage Tailwind v4 properly. `base.css` contains ~500 lines of utility classes that duplicate Tailwind v4 natives (flex, grid, gap-*, p-*, m-*, shadow-*, etc.). Because `@import "tailwindcss"` comes AFTER these definitions in the cascade, Tailwind OVERRIDES most of them anyway — meaning ~500 lines of dead weight that don't work as intended.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Audit every class in `base.css` against Tailwind v4 defaults
- Remove duplicate utilities that Tailwind already provides
- Preserve semantic/color utilities that reference CSS custom properties (unique to this project)
- Preserve layout utilities (`max-w-container-max`, `px-margin-mobile`, `px-margin-desktop`, `py-gutter`) that use project tokens
- Fix import order in `index.css` so Tailwind and custom CSS play well together
- Verify visual output is identical after refactor

### Out of Scope
- JSX/React component changes
- `tokens.css` (already clean and unique)
- `utilities.css` (mostly unique premium effects)
- New features or design changes

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- None

### Modified Capabilities
- `landing-design-tokens`: CSS structure within the design system changes, but token values and theme stay the same

## Approach

1. **Audit `base.css` utilities** — Categorize each class as:
   - `REMOVE` — duplicates Tailwind v4 native (e.g., `.flex`, `.gap-4`, `.p-6`, `.shadow-lg`)
   - `KEEP` — uses project tokens or serves semantic purpose (e.g., `.bg-gold-gradient-bg`, `.max-w-container-max`)
   - `MOVE` — duplicates that need project-specific values retained in `utilities.css`

2. **Fix import order in `index.css`** — Tailwind v4 `@import "tailwindcss"` must come BEFORE custom CSS so native utilities win; custom overrides come after for exceptions only

3. **Consolidate semantic utilities** — Color/border/text utilities that reference CSS vars (`--gold`, `--navy-900`, etc.) move to `utilities.css` under a `/* Semantic Overrides */` section

4. **Verify** — `pnpm build` succeeds, visual output unchanged

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/index.css` | Modified | Fix import order — `@import "tailwindcss"` moves to line 1 (before custom imports) |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/base.css` | Removed | ~500 lines of duplicated utilities removed; ~50 unique custom classes preserved |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/utilities.css` | Modified | Receive semantic color utilities migrated from base.css |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Missed usage of a removed class in JSX | Low | Run full grep for every removed class before delete; revert if build fails |
| Import order fix breaks specificity | Low | Tailwind v4 resets cascade at import; test with `pnpm dev` before commit |
| Accidentally removing a class Tailwind doesn't cover | Low | Manual audit of each section; all hardcoded-value classes (not matching Tailwind defaults) are preserved |

## Rollback Plan

```bash
git checkout HEAD -- lawyerPortfolio/src/index.css lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/base.css lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/utilities.css
```
Single git revert restores all files.

## Dependencies

- Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`)
- No external dependencies

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `pnpm build` succeeds without errors
- [ ] Visual output in browser is byte-for-byte identical (no visible changes)
- [ ] `base.css` reduced from ~1033 lines to ~150 lines
- [ ] No duplicate Tailwind utility classes remain in `base.css`
- [ ] Import order in `index.css` places Tailwind before custom CSS

observations.title: sdd/css-architecture-cleanup/design
observations.content:
# Design: CSS Architecture Cleanup

## Technical Approach

Remove ~500 lines of duplicate Tailwind v4 utilities from `base.css` (lines 184–1033) while preserving two categories: (1) semantic utilities referencing project CSS tokens, and (2) responsive container/layout classes that control exact pixel dimensions. Fix import order so Tailwind's base layer is established before custom CSS loads.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: Container Size Protection

**Choice**: Explicitly enumerate every container-affecting class and audit line-by-line against the removal list. Apply a "keep list" policy for any class using `--container-max`, `--margin-mobile`, `--margin-desktop`, or `--gutter`.

**Keep list (MUST NOT TOUCH)**:
| Class | Line | Token Used | Purpose |
|-------|------|------------|---------|
| `.max-w-container-max` | 328 | `--container-max` | Max content width (1280px) |
| `.px-margin-mobile` | 334 | `--margin-mobile` | Horizontal padding mobile (1rem) |
| `.px-margin-desktop` | 339 | `--margin-desktop` | Horizontal padding desktop (2rem) |
| `.py-gutter` | 344 | `--gutter` | Vertical gutter (1.5rem) |

### Decision: Import Order — `@import "tailwindcss"` First

**New order**: Tailwind first, then fonts, then tokens.css, base.css, utilities.css.
**Rationale**: Tailwind v4's `@import "tailwindcss"` registers `@layer base` at the correct cascade position. Custom CSS placed BEFORE Tailwind ends up outside `@layer base` and wins the cascade unintentionally.

### Decision: Semantic Utilities to Preserve

Keep color/border/text utilities that reference CSS custom properties (`--gold`, `--navy-900`, `--surface`, etc.) even if class name resembles a Tailwind pattern. These are project-specific semantic tokens — removing them breaks the design system.

### Decision: Responsive Utilities Are Not Duplicates

`.md\:flex`, `.md\:hidden`, `.md\:grid-cols-2`, `.md\:grid-cols-3`, `.md\:col-span-2`, `.lg\:grid-cols-2` are valid Tailwind v4 responsive variants (md/lg breakpoint prefixes). Preserved.

## Exact Line Ranges for base.css

| Lines | Action | Count | Reason |
|-------|--------|-------|---------|
| 184–327 | KEEP | 144 | Base styles (reset, typography, scrollbar, focus, reduced-motion, semantic utilities) |
| 328–347 | KEEP | 20 | **CRITICAL** container classes |
| 348–1033 | REMOVE | 686 | Duplicate Tailwind v4 utilities |
| 1024–1029 | KEEP | 6 | Scroll-margin-top for sticky navbar anchor offset |

## File Changes

| File | Action | Change |
|------|--------|--------|
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/index.css` | Modify | Move `@import "tailwindcss"` to line 1 |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/base.css` | Modify | Remove lines 348–1033 (except 1024–1029) |
| `lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/utilities.css` | No-op | No changes |

## Rollback

```bash
git checkout HEAD -- lawyerPortfolio/src/index.css lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/base.css lawyerPortfolio/src/styles/utilities.css
```

## Open Questions

- [ ] Should duplicate responsive utilities (`.items-center` appears at lines 375 and 838) be consolidated?
- [ ] Should dark-mode surface overrides from `tokens.css` `.dark {}` block be documented as out-of-scope?
